title: Are blocks with non-empty ommers properly rejected at the P2P boundary in post-merge Osaka fork?

phase1_result.abstract_domain: Post-merge consensus validation domain. State space: S = {(header, block_body) | header.difficulty == 0}. Two validation predicates: P1(block) := len(block.Uncles()) == 0 (body validation) and P2(header) := header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash (header validation). Safety property: ∀ block ∈ post_merge_blocks: P1(block) ∧ P2(header) must hold.
phase1_result.abstract_state_transitions: Block processing pipeline: P2P Reception → Header Verification (VerifyHeaders @ line 1785 blockchain.go → verifyHeader @ line 222-232 consensus.go checks UncleHash) → Body Validation (ValidateBody @ line 64 block_validator.go → VerifyUncles @ line 201 consensus.go checks len(Uncles())). Transition guards ensure: (1) header.UncleHash != EmptyUncleHash → reject with errInvalidUncleHash (line 231-232), (2) len(block.Uncles()) > 0 → reject with errTooManyUncles (line 206-207).
phase1_result.potential_violations: Potential violation vectors: (1) Race condition between header and body validation - MITIGATED: header validated first in parallel (line 1785), body validated sequentially (line 64 block_validator.go). (2) Execution engine bypass via Engine API - REQUIRES ANALYSIS: ExecutableDataToBlock (line 667 api.go) constructs blocks from CL payloads. (3) Uncle hash computation mismatch - MITIGATED: CalcUncleHash(block.Uncles()) compared against header.UncleHash (line 67 block_validator.go).
phase1_result.summary: Two independent validation layers exist: header-level (UncleHash constant check) and body-level (uncles list length check). Both execute on all post-merge blocks. Header validation occurs during parallel VerifyHeaders phase; body validation occurs during sequential ValidateBody phase. No obvious gaps in validation chain.

phase2_result.reachability_path: POST-MERGE BLOCKS: P2P path disabled (handleNewBlock returns error line 350). Engine API path: CL → NewPayloadV4 → ExecutableDataToBlock (beacon/engine/types.go:279 hardcodes UncleHash: types.EmptyUncleHash, line 300 sets Uncles: nil) → InsertBlockWithoutSetHead (blockchain.go:2558) → insertChain (line 1785: VerifyHeaders → verifyHeader line 231-232 checks UncleHash) → ValidateBody (block_validator.go:64 calls VerifyUncles line 206-207). CRITICAL: Engine API blocks have UncleHash and Uncles set at construction time (types.go:279, 300), then validated during insertion.
phase2_result.symbolic_constraints: Let B = block received. Path constraints: C1 := B.header.difficulty == 0 (IsPoSHeader check), C2 := B.header.UncleHash (value from network/CL), C3 := len(B.body.Uncles) (value from network/CL). Validation constraints: V1 := (C2 == EmptyUncleHash), V2 := (C3 == 0), V3 := CalcUncleHash(B.body.Uncles) == C2. Block accepted IFF C1 ∧ V1 ∧ V2 ∧ V3. Symbolic execution: If C2 != EmptyUncleHash → errInvalidUncleHash at line 232. If C3 > 0 → errTooManyUncles at line 207. If V3 fails → mismatch error at line 67 block_validator.go.
phase2_result.feasibility: INFEASIBLE to bypass. Proof by path enumeration: (1) P2P path: disabled post-merge (line 350 handlers.go). (2) Engine API path: UncleHash hardcoded to EmptyUncleHash at construction (types.go:279), Uncles hardcoded to nil (line 300). Even if malicious CL sends non-empty uncle data in ExecutableData, block construction forces empty values. (3) Direct insertion: insertChain always calls VerifyHeaders (line 1785) before ValidateBody. (4) Known block optimization: skipBlock (line 1793) only skips if block known AND behind current head - validation already occurred. No feasible path exists to insert post-merge block with non-empty uncles.
phase2_result.summary: All entry points converge to mandatory validation. P2P disabled for post-merge. Engine API enforces empty ommers at block construction time (beacon/engine/types.go:279, 300) before validation. Validation occurs in two phases: parallel header verification (checks UncleHash constant) and sequential body validation (checks uncles list empty + hash match). No bypass vectors identified.

phase3_result.proof_sketch: INVARIANT: ∀ b ∈ post_merge_blocks: b.header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash ∧ len(b.Uncles()) == 0. PROOF BY INDUCTION: Base case: Genesis block after merge satisfies invariant (difficulty == 0 → PoS rules apply). Inductive step: Assume chain up to block N satisfies invariant. For block N+1: (1) Construction phase: If via Engine API, ExecutableDataToBlock hardcodes UncleHash=EmptyUncleHash (line 279) and Uncles=nil (line 300). (2) Validation phase: verifyHeader checks header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash (line 231-232), rejects otherwise. VerifyUncles checks len(block.Uncles()) == 0 (line 206-207), rejects otherwise. ValidateBody checks CalcUncleHash(Uncles) == header.UncleHash (line 67), rejects if mismatch. (3) Acceptance: Block accepted → all validations passed → invariant holds for N+1. By induction, invariant holds for all post-merge blocks. CONSISTENCY: Both header and body validations are mandatory (not conditional), execute on BeaconConsensusEngine for all PoS blocks (difficulty==0 check at line 202, 228).
phase3_result.summary: Invariant HOLDS with high confidence. Multiple defense layers: (1) Construction enforcement (Engine API hardcodes empty values), (2) Header validation (UncleHash constant check), (3) Body validation (length check), (4) Consistency validation (hash recomputation). All validations mandatory for post-merge blocks. P2P propagation disabled. No conditional branches that could skip validation.

justification: SAFE - The invariant that post-merge blocks must have empty ommers is enforced through multiple mandatory validation layers: (1) beacon/engine/types.go:279,300 hardcodes UncleHash=EmptyUncleHash and Uncles=nil during block construction from execution payloads, (2) consensus/beacon/consensus.go:231-232 validates header.UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash in verifyHeader, (3) consensus/beacon/consensus.go:206-207 validates len(block.Uncles())==0 in VerifyUncles, (4) core/block_validator.go:67 validates CalcUncleHash matches header.UncleHash. All validation layers are mandatory (no conditional skips) and execute for all post-merge blocks (difficulty==0). P2P block propagation disabled post-merge (eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go:350). No feasible bypass vectors identified. High confidence due to defense-in-depth approach.

title: Does actor-p2p-peer correctly validate ommers_hash equals EMPTY_OMMER_HASH before forwarding blocks?

phase1_result.abstract_domain: P2P network boundary validation domain. Actor model: P2P_PEER receives block B from network. State space: S = {received_block, validated_block, forwarded_block, rejected_block}. Validation predicate at boundary: V_boundary(B) := B.header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash. Safety property: ∀ B ∈ received_blocks: ¬V_boundary(B) → B ∉ forwarded_blocks.
phase1_result.abstract_state_transitions: Network reception flow: Peer_Network → handleMessage (eth/protocols/eth/handler.go:200) → handleNewBlock (line 349) → FOR POST-MERGE: error 'block broadcasts disallowed' (line 350). FOR PRE-MERGE (not applicable): Backend.Handle → InsertChain → VerifyHeaders. State transitions: received → [validation] → {accepted, rejected}. For post-merge blocks, transition is: received → rejected (P2P disabled).
phase1_result.potential_violations: Potential violation vectors: (1) P2P broadcast of post-merge blocks - STATUS: Explicitly disabled (line 350 handlers.go). (2) Block bodies received via BlockBodiesMsg without header validation - MITIGATED: Body responses are matched to requests (line 373-378 handlers.go), headers validated separately. (3) Sync mode bypass (snap sync, fast sync) - REQUIRES ANALYSIS: Different sync paths may have different validation. (4) Trusted peer bypass - REQUIRES ANALYSIS: No evidence of trusted peer validation skip.
phase1_result.summary: P2P broadcast mechanism for blocks (NewBlockMsg) is explicitly disabled for post-merge networks (line 350 returns error). Block propagation post-merge occurs via consensus layer (CL), not P2P eth protocol. Historical validation for pre-merge blocks still active but not relevant for post-merge Osaka fork scope.

phase2_result.reachability_path: P2P BLOCK RECEPTION PATH: Peer → msg reception (handler.go:200-236) → handleNewBlock (line 349) → IMMEDIATE RETURN with error 'block broadcasts disallowed' (line 350). ANALYSIS: go-ethereum dropped support for pre-merge networks, so NewBlockMsg is disabled. Post-merge block propagation: CL receives blocks from beacon network → Engine API (NewPayloadV*) → ExecutableDataToBlock → validation. HEADERS PATH: handleBlockHeaders (line 353) → peer.dispatchResponse (line 366-370) → response matching for sync requests only, not unsolicited. BODIES PATH: handleBlockBodies (line 373) → peer.dispatchResponse → matched to previous GetBlockBodies request. CONCLUSION: No unsolicited P2P forwarding path exists for post-merge blocks.
phase2_result.symbolic_constraints: Let M = received message. Path constraints: C1 := M.Code (message type), C2 := M.Size <= maxMessageSize (line 206). For NewBlockMsg (code 0x07): Handler = handleNewBlock → ALWAYS returns error (line 350), no validation performed, no forwarding occurs. For sync-based reception (BlockHeadersMsg, BlockBodiesMsg): Constraints: C3 := response matches pending request ID, C4 := headers validated via VerifyHeaders before insertion. Symbolic execution shows: NewBlockMsg path has NO reachable state where block is forwarded without validation, because forwarding code is unreachable (error returned immediately).
phase2_result.feasibility: NOT APPLICABLE for property evaluation. The property asks whether P2P peers validate ommers_hash before forwarding. Analysis shows: (1) Post-merge blocks are NOT propagated via P2P eth protocol at all (line 350 disables NewBlockMsg). (2) Block sync (headers/bodies) is request-response based, not forwarding. (3) Forwarding would require acceptance → insertion → broadcast, but handleNewBlock prevents acceptance. FEASIBILITY OF VIOLATION: INFEASIBLE - no P2P forwarding mechanism exists for post-merge blocks.
phase2_result.summary: P2P forwarding of post-merge blocks does not exist in go-ethereum post-merge architecture. Block propagation moved to consensus layer. The eth/68 and eth/69 protocols disable unsolicited block broadcasts (line 350). Therefore, the question of whether P2P peers validate before forwarding is NOT APPLICABLE - there is no forwarding to validate.

phase3_result.proof_sketch: INVARIANT (adapted): ∀ B ∈ post_merge_blocks received via P2P: B is NOT forwarded via P2P (forwarding disabled). ORIGINAL PROPERTY (validation before forwarding): Not directly applicable since forwarding disabled. PROOF: (1) Post-merge architecture change: Block propagation moved from execution layer P2P (eth protocol) to consensus layer (beacon network). Evidence: eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go:346 'block announcements disallowed', line 350 'block broadcasts disallowed'. (2) Code path analysis: handleNewBlock (line 349-351) is the only handler for unsolicited block messages (NewBlockMsg). Function body: return errors.New('block broadcasts disallowed'). No conditional logic, no validation, no forwarding. (3) Alternative paths: Block sync (headers+bodies) is request-response, not forwarding. Sync path validates headers (VerifyHeaders) and bodies (ValidateBody) during insertion, but does not forward. (4) CONCLUSION: The property 'validate before forwarding' is vacuously true - since no forwarding occurs, the implication (forward → validated) holds trivially.
phase3_result.summary: Property is OUT-OF-SCOPE for post-merge architecture. P2P forwarding of blocks does not exist - block propagation occurs via consensus layer. The eth protocol handlers explicitly disable block broadcasts (line 350). While header validation (including UncleHash check) occurs during block insertion from Engine API, this is not 'P2P peer forwarding'. The invariant that could be evaluated is: 'P2P peers do not forward post-merge blocks' which HOLDS by design (forwarding disabled).

justification: OUT-OF-SCOPE - The property asks whether P2P peers validate ommers_hash before forwarding blocks. Analysis reveals this is not applicable to post-merge go-ethereum architecture: (1) Block propagation via P2P eth protocol is explicitly disabled post-merge (eth/protocols/eth/handlers.go:350 returns error for NewBlockMsg), (2) Post-merge blocks propagate via consensus layer (beacon network) to execution layer via Engine API, not P2P eth protocol, (3) No code path exists for P2P forwarding of post-merge blocks. The header validation (UncleHash check at consensus/beacon/consensus.go:231-232) does occur, but in the Engine API insertion path, not P2P forwarding path. High confidence in out-of-scope classification due to explicit architectural change documented in code comments and handler implementations.

title: Does actor-execution-engine enforce the empty ommers invariant during block execution?

phase1_result.abstract_domain: Execution engine block processing domain. Actor: EXECUTION_ENGINE receives execution payloads from consensus layer. State space: S = {payload_received, block_constructed, block_validated, block_executed, state_updated}. Enforcement mechanisms: (1) Construction-time enforcement: payload → block conversion sets UncleHash=EmptyUncleHash, Uncles=nil. (2) Validation-time enforcement: VerifyUncles, verifyHeader validate ommers empty. Safety property: ∀ payload ∈ execution_payloads: constructed_block(payload).Uncles == [] ∧ constructed_block(payload).UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash.
phase1_result.abstract_state_transitions: Engine API flow: CL → NewPayloadV* (eth/catalyst/api.go:625) → ExecutableDataToBlock (beacon/engine/types.go:200-303) → block construction [line 279: UncleHash=EmptyUncleHash, line 300: Uncles=nil] → InsertBlockWithoutSetHead (core/blockchain.go:2558) → insertChain (line 1785: VerifyHeaders, line 1789: ValidateBody) → execution → state update. State transitions enforce invariant at TWO points: construction (hardcoded) and validation (checked).
phase1_result.potential_violations: Potential violation vectors: (1) Malicious CL sends ExecutableData with uncle-related fields - MITIGATED: ExecutableData struct does not have uncle fields (beacon/engine/types.go), block construction ignores any such data. (2) Direct block construction bypass - INFEASIBLE: NewPayloadV* is the only Engine API entry point, always calls ExecutableDataToBlock. (3) Validation skip during execution - MITIGATED: insertChain (line 1785) always calls VerifyHeaders before execution. (4) Uncle reward distribution in execution - ANALYZED: Beacon.Finalize (consensus.go:339-352) has NO uncle reward code (unlike ethone.Finalize), comment line 351 'No block reward which is issued by consensus layer instead'.
phase1_result.summary: Execution engine enforces empty ommers through construction-time hardcoding (beacon/engine/types.go:279,300) AND validation-time checking (VerifyHeaders→verifyHeader checks UncleHash, VerifyUncles checks Uncles list). Block execution (Finalize) does not process uncles or distribute uncle rewards.

phase2_result.reachability_path: EXECUTION ENGINE PATH: CL beacon node → Engine API RPC → NewPayloadV4(params ExecutableData, ...) (api.go:625) → [line 649-660: lock acquisition, method tracking] → line 667: ExecutableDataToBlock(params, versionedHashes, beaconRoot, requests) → [CONSTRUCTION: types.go:277-300 creates header with UncleHash=EmptyUncleHash line 279, creates body with Uncles=nil line 300] → line 711: InsertBlockWithoutSetHead(block) → [VALIDATION: blockchain.go:2558 calls insertChain → line 1785: engine.VerifyHeaders validates UncleHash, block_validator.go:64 VerifyUncles validates Uncles list] → [EXECUTION: blockchain.go processes txs, calls Finalize] → consensus.go:339 Finalize → [lines 345-350: withdrawal processing only, NO uncle processing] → state update committed.
phase2_result.symbolic_constraints: Let P = ExecutableData payload. Construction constraints: B.header.UncleHash := EmptyUncleHash (constant assignment line 279), B.body.Uncles := nil (constant assignment line 300). These are UNCONDITIONAL assignments, not dependent on payload content. Validation constraints during insertion: V1 := (B.header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash) checked line 231, V2 := (len(B.body.Uncles) == 0) checked line 206, V3 := (CalcUncleHash(B.body.Uncles) == B.header.UncleHash) checked line 67 block_validator.go. Execution constraints: Finalize iterates over B.body.Withdrawals (line 345), does NOT iterate over B.body.Uncles. Symbolic execution: Path from P to state update ALWAYS includes construction (sets empty) AND validation (checks empty) AND execution (ignores uncles field). No conditional branches that skip these steps.
phase2_result.feasibility: VIOLATION INFEASIBLE. Proof by construction and validation analysis: (1) CONSTRUCTION PHASE: ExecutableDataToBlock creates block with hardcoded empty uncle values (line 279, 300). Even if malicious CL includes uncle data in ExecutableData fields, the conversion function DOES NOT READ such fields (ExecutableData struct has no uncle-related fields per types.go:38-71). Block constructed with Uncles=nil by definition. (2) VALIDATION PHASE: Constructed block passes through insertChain which calls VerifyHeaders (checks UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash) and ValidateBody→VerifyUncles (checks len(Uncles)==0). Both validations mandatory. (3) EXECUTION PHASE: Finalize processes withdrawals but not uncles (no iteration over Uncles, no uncle rewards). (4) CONCLUSION: No executable path exists where execution engine accepts/processes block with non-empty uncles.
phase2_result.summary: Execution engine enforces empty ommers invariant through defense-in-depth: (1) Construction enforcement - hardcoded constant values during payload-to-block conversion, (2) Validation enforcement - mandatory checks during block insertion, (3) Execution behavior - Finalize does not process uncles. All phases mandatory, no bypass vectors identified.

phase3_result.proof_sketch: INVARIANT: Execution engine enforces ∀ b ∈ executed_blocks: b.header.UncleHash == EmptyUncleHash ∧ len(b.Uncles()) == 0 ∧ no_uncle_rewards_distributed. PROOF BY PHASE ANALYSIS: (1) CONSTRUCTION PHASE ENFORCEMENT: ExecutableDataToBlock (types.go:200-303) creates block header with UncleHash field assigned EmptyUncleHash constant (line 279), creates block body with Uncles field assigned nil (line 300). These are direct field assignments, not conditional. Code path analysis: NewPayloadV* → ExecutableDataToBlock (line 667) is ONLY path for Engine API block construction. LEMMA 1: ∀ blocks constructed via Engine API: UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash ∧ Uncles==nil. (2) VALIDATION PHASE ENFORCEMENT: InsertBlockWithoutSetHead → insertChain (line 2558, 1785) calls engine.VerifyHeaders. For PoS blocks (difficulty==0), routes to beacon.verifyHeader (line 124) which checks header.UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash (line 231-232). insertChain also validates via ValidateBody → VerifyUncles (block_validator.go:64, consensus.go:201) which checks len(block.Uncles())==0 (line 206-207). Both validations mandatory, no conditional skip. LEMMA 2: ∀ blocks inserted into chain: passed validation → UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash ∧ len(Uncles)==0. (3) EXECUTION PHASE ENFORCEMENT: Block execution calls Finalize (consensus.go:339). Function processes withdrawals (line 345-350) but has no code path for uncle processing. Comment line 351: 'No block reward which is issued by consensus layer instead'. LEMMA 3: ∀ blocks executed: no uncle rewards distributed. CONCLUSION: Invariant HOLDS by construction (LEMMA 1), validation (LEMMA 2), and execution behavior (LEMMA 3).
phase3_result.summary: Invariant HOLDS with high confidence. Execution engine enforces empty ommers through three independent mechanisms: (1) Construction-time hardcoding (beacon/engine/types.go:279,300), (2) Validation-time checking (consensus/beacon/consensus.go:231,206 and block_validator.go:67), (3) Execution-time non-processing (consensus/beacon/consensus.go:339-352 Finalize has no uncle logic). All mechanisms are mandatory for post-merge blocks processed via Engine API.

justification: SAFE - The execution engine enforces the empty ommers invariant through multiple mandatory mechanisms: (1) CONSTRUCTION: beacon/engine/types.go:279 hardcodes header.UncleHash=types.EmptyUncleHash and line 300 hardcodes body.Uncles=nil when converting ExecutableData to Block, (2) VALIDATION: core/blockchain.go:1785 calls VerifyHeaders which routes to consensus/beacon/consensus.go:231-232 checking UncleHash==EmptyUncleHash, and core/block_validator.go:64 calls VerifyUncles which checks len(Uncles())==0 at line 206-207, (3) EXECUTION: consensus/beacon/consensus.go:339-352 Finalize processes withdrawals but has no uncle processing logic (comment line 351 confirms no block reward). All three phases are mandatory for blocks received via Engine API (the only post-merge block source). No conditional branches that skip enforcement. High confidence due to defense-in-depth across construction, validation, and execution phases.
